item: 3.8 edit the Bash command in the permission card — editable in place, the edit rides Accept as updatedInput (2026-09-05)
branch: previewHtml renders `.cmd` with contenteditable=plaintext-only and data-orig when the input has a `command` shown WHOLE (a cut command and a description-only preview stay read-only). An input event toggles `.cmd-edited` on the card while the text differs from data-orig. Always-allow and the destination rows stay on every card and grant the EDITED text — done() keeps the suggestion with its chip rewritten, Kotlin (EditProposals.withRulesFor) rewrites the echoed rules to one exact rule per part of the edited command (splitCommand). On a COMPOUND card (`.cmd-compound`) the per-rule rows and their header hide while edited, since they name the original parts. done(true) sends the edited text as `cmd` on the bridge perm message, drops any suggestion, removes the editability and says `edited in the IDE before accepting` on the decided line. Kotlin (EditProposals.withCommand) replaces `command` in the input the CLI asked about.
provenance: Wire: PROBED 2026-09-05 (2.1.260, stdio): allowing a `factor 97` ask with updatedInput.command=`factor 91` ran `factor 91` (tool_result `91: 7 13`); the transcript keeps the ORIGINAL command in the tool_use and only the output in the result, so the edit is live-only on replay. VS Code renders the command contentEditable and sends the edit as updatedInput (checklist 3.8). Negative control on the pre-3.8 build: no `.cmd[contenteditable]` exists, so the editable/edited/cmd-on-the-wire asserts read 'absent' or 0 — DISCRIMINATING; the untouched-accept and over-cap asserts are GUARDS on both builds. Rewritten rule PROBED 2026-09-05 (2.1.260, trusted scratch workspace): echoing the suggestion with ruleContent `factor 91` persisted `Bash(factor 91)` to settings.local.json; the next `factor 91` did not ask, `factor 97` still did. A rule for a WHOLE compound string is persisted but never matches (the CLI checks parts separately; probed the same day), hence the per-part split; a bare `&` compound still asks every time regardless of rules (probed: `factor 91 & factor 95` re-asked with an EMPTY suggestion list, i.e. both parts already allowed).
